title: Problem solving: draw a picture
summary: Read the problem. Say what you know and what you need to find. Draw it, then solve it.
guide: Solving a problem has four steps: 1. understand the problem (what do we know, what are we asked?), 2. choose a strategy, 3. solve it, 4. look back and check the answer. This studio practises one {{term:problem-solving-strategy}}: draw a picture.
In step 1 the child taps the facts needed to solve the problem and picks the question. Some problems include a number that is not needed; spotting it is part of understanding the problem.

The picture is a simple bar model: one bar for the whole with its parts underneath, or two bars to compare. It does not need to be a drawing of the real things; simple shapes are enough. The child picks up a number and puts it in its place, and puts ? where the number is not known.

The first mission suits Year 1: the answer is a number tile, so no typing is needed. Read the problem aloud if your child is not reading yet. Step 4, looking back, is the "why" question at the end of each mission.

engine.label-known: What do we know? Tap the facts you need.
engine.instruction-draw: Tap a number, then tap its place in the picture.
engine.ask-sara-now: How many apples does Sara have now?
engine.ask-ali-gave: How many apples did Ali give?
engine.ask-science: How many science books does Ali have?
engine.ask-all-books: How many books does Ali have altogether?
engine.fact-fewer-6: Hassan has 6 fewer pencils than Maryam.
engine.ask-hasan: How many pencils does Hassan have?
engine.ask-difference: How many more pencils does Maryam have?
engine.ask-start: How many stickers did Zahra have at first?
engine.ask-gave: How many stickers did Zahra give away?

join.title: How many altogether?
join.prompt: Sara has 5 apples. Ali gives her 3 apples. How many apples does Sara have now?
join.hint: Sara's apples and Ali's apples are the two parts. We don't know the whole, so put ? there.
join.success: Well done! 5 apples and 3 apples make 8 apples. 5 + 3 = 8
join.why: Use the picture: why is the answer more than 5?
join.model: Because the top bar is all the apples: Sara's 5 and Ali's 3 together. The whole is always more than each part. To check: 8 − 3 = 5, Sara's apples at the start.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap both numbers in the problem.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that. What does it not tell us?
feedback.bar-empty: Tap a number, then tap its place in the picture.
feedback.bar-whole: The top bar is the whole: all the apples. We don't know it yet, so put ? there.
feedback.bar-parts: In the two parts underneath, put Sara's apples and Ali's apples.
feedback.took-away: Ali gave apples, so Sara has more, not fewer.
feedback.start: 5 is what Sara had at the start. Count Ali's 3 as well.

part-unknown.title: How many are left?
part-unknown.prompt: Ali has 23 books. The books are on 2 shelves. 12 are storybooks and the rest are science books. How many science books does Ali have?
part-unknown.hint: The whole is 23 books. One part is the 12 storybooks. We don't know the other part.
part-unknown.success: Well done! 23 − 12 = 11. Ali has 11 science books.
part-unknown.why: Did you need the 2 shelves? Why or why not? How can you check your answer?
part-unknown.model: No. The question is about how many books, not shelves. To check, I add the parts: 12 + 11 = 23, which is all the books.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap all the books and the storybooks.
feedback.known-extra: Do you need the number of shelves to find the science books?
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem tells us how many books there are altogether. What don't we know?
feedback.bar-empty: Tap a number, then tap its place in the picture.
feedback.bar-whole: The top bar is the whole: all of Ali's books. Which number is all the books?
feedback.bar-parts: The two parts are storybooks and science books. Which one don't we know? Put ? there.
feedback.added: 35 is more than all the books! The science books are part of the 23 books.
feedback.shelves: The shelves don't matter here. Use only 23 and 12.
feedback.too-big: The science part and 12 must make 23. Work it out again.
feedback.too-small: The science part and 12 must make 23. Work it out again.
feedback.empty: Write the answer in the gap.

compare.title: How many fewer?
compare.prompt: Maryam has 14 pencils. Hassan has 6 fewer pencils than Maryam. How many pencils does Hassan have?
compare.hint: First say who has more. Hassan's bar is shorter; the dashed piece is the difference.
compare.why: The problem said "fewer". How did the picture stop you from adding by mistake?
compare.model: In the picture Hassan's bar is shorter than Maryam's, so the answer must be less than 14. 8 and 6 make 14: if Hassan had 6 more pencils, he would have the same as Maryam.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap both numbers in the problem.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem tells us "6 fewer". What don't we know?
feedback.bar-more: Read it again: Hassan has 6 fewer pencils than Maryam. So who has more?
feedback.bar-empty: Tap a number, then tap its place in the picture.
feedback.bar-parts: Put Maryam's pencils in Maryam's bar. We don't know Hassan's, so put ? there.
feedback.bar-diff: The dashed piece is the gap between the bars: how many fewer does Hassan have?
feedback.added: Hassan has fewer than Maryam, so the answer must be less than 14.
feedback.too-big: Look at Hassan's bar: 14 take away the dashed piece.
feedback.too-small: Look at Hassan's bar: 14 take away the dashed piece.
feedback.empty: Write the answer in the gap.

start-unknown.title: How many at first?
start-unknown.prompt: Zahra had some stickers. She gave 5 stickers to Fatima. Now she has 9 stickers. How many stickers did Zahra have at first?
start-unknown.hint: Zahra's first stickers split into two parts: the ones she gave and the ones she kept. Which is the whole?
start-unknown.success: Well done! 9 + 5 = 14. Zahra had 14 stickers at first.
start-unknown.why: The problem said "gave", but we added. Why? Check your answer.
start-unknown.model: Because Zahra's first stickers are the whole: the 9 she kept and the 5 she gave. To check: 14 − 5 = 9, the stickers she has left.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap both numbers in the problem.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that. What don't we know?
feedback.bar-empty: Tap a number, then tap its place in the picture.
feedback.bar-whole: The top bar is the stickers Zahra had at first. We don't know that, so put ? there.
feedback.bar-parts: The two parts are the stickers she gave and the stickers she kept.
feedback.took-away: If Zahra had only 4 stickers, how could she give away 5? Look at the picture: which is the whole?
feedback.too-big: The whole is made of the parts 9 and 5. Work it out again.
feedback.too-small: The whole is made of the parts 9 and 5. Work it out again.
feedback.empty: Write the answer in the gap.
